content.what_it_is: Python/Matplotlib sediment-rip frame plotter. It derives the case output directory from HOME, loads baseline depth, and builds a dx=1,dy=2 mesh (L13-L35); takes an inclusive frame range (L37-L41); loads u/v/eta/mask/concentration/evolving depth and computes depth change (L44-L60); then draws eta, log10 concentration with quiver, and depth-change contour panels and saves/shows a PNG (L62-L126).
unresolved: `depp` is calculated at L54 before current masking, while only eta, baseline dep, u, and v are masked at L57-L60; concentration and evolving depth/depth change remain unmasked, so dry/sentinel values appear in panels 2 and 3 while panel 1 and arrows hide them.

Baseline `dep` is mutated to NaN at L58 and never restored. On the next frame, depp=dep1-dep at L54 already inherits all historical dry NaNs, and further masking accumulates, making multi-frame depth changes history-dependent.
`np.log10(ch)` at L86 lacks a positivity/missing-value guard; zeros become -Inf and negatives become NaN, inconsistent with the finite [-1,1] display range.
There is no figure/axes clear or close inside L41-L126, so artists and newly created colorbar axes accumulate across frames.
All panels crop x to 7/9 of the loaded domain at L69,L103,L114 without explanation; HOME, inputs, file existence, and cross-array shapes are unvalidated.
